title: Scale library to 10 or more plans across units
context: M2's exit criterion requires at least 10 lesson plans published cumulatively, with at least 5 adopted. This task represents the authoring work to reach that scale: expanding beyond the M1 unit to cover additional subjects, grade bands, or topics, with all plans passing both gates and emitting valid metadata. Scale also generates the cycle-time data (author-to-review-to-delivery time per plan) needed to benchmark and improve the process. The full M2 toolchain (PDF exporter, CC exporter, CASE/LRMI metadata) must be in place so every plan in this batch is fully interoperable.
objective: Author and deliver enough lesson plans to reach 10 or more cumulatively published plans (across M0-M2), with at least 5 adopted by real teachers or repositories, and cycle-time data recorded.
acceptanceCriteria: At least 10 lesson plans are published cumulatively (counting plans from pilot-008 and unit-012), each passing both the license gate and the pedagogy/standards review gate with committed artifacts.
CASE/LRMI metadata is emitted and validates for every plan (teacher-lesson-plans-casemeta-011); PDF/HTML and Common Cartridge exports are produced for every plan.
At least 5 of the 10+ plans are adopted: taught by a real teacher or accepted by an OER repository, with adoption evidence committed to the outcome ledger.
Author-to-review-to-delivery cycle time is recorded for each plan in this batch and an aggregate baseline is computed and committed.
Plans in this batch cover at least one additional subject, grade band, or thematic unit beyond the M1 unit, demonstrating breadth.
Commits are DCO signed-off; no secrets or PII in committed files.
resources: teacher-lesson-plans-unit-012 — M1 unit (starting point for M2 expansion)
teacher-lesson-plans-template-001 — canonical lesson-plan schema and template
OER sources: OpenStax, CK-12, OER Commons, Curriki, Siyavula
output: 10 or more cumulatively published lesson plans (in Markdown + gate artifacts + metadata + exports), at least 5 with adoption evidence, and a committed cycle-time baseline report.
